mechanism_narrative: As the peak summer holiday period concludes in Lombardy, the gradual return of residents from vacation will lead to increased out-of-home activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people resume normal routines.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days, despite a decrease in RESIDENTIAL and an increase in WORKPLACES mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained increase in PARKS mobility, reaching 14.4% above baseline, indicates a growing public willingness to engage in outdoor leisure. This increased out-of-home activity will translate into higher RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility remains above 10% and shows a positive week-on-week change
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not increase, despite PARKS mobility remaining above 10% and rising.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent low and slightly declining WORKPLACES mobility, currently at -39.6%, suggests a continued lack of return to physical offices. This will suppress weekday retail and recreation activity, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases significantly, despite WORKPLACES mobility remaining below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility, consistently above 6% baseline, indicates people are spending more time at home. This directly reduces opportunities for out-of-home retail and recreation, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 5% of baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises by more than 2 percentage points while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT stations mobility would signal improved public transport usage, facilitating greater access to retail and recreation venues and boosting RETAIL_REC within the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT mobility rises by more than 1.5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility rises by more than 1.5 percentage points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase within the subsequent 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: A combined pattern of persistently low WORKPLACES mobility and elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility signifies a strong work-from-home or extended holiday pattern that will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks due to reduced daily commutes and out-of-home leisure.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases by more than 3 percentage points while WORKPLACES remains below -35% and RESIDENTIAL remains above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: The stable but below-baseline GROCERY_PHARM mobility suggests that essential activities are not significantly increasing. This implies no underlying surge in general out-of-home activity that would drive RETAIL_REC up over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains within +/- 0.5 percentage points of its current level (-22.4%)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points over the next 14 days, despite GROCERY_PHARM mobility remaining stable.

mechanism_narrative: The recent uptick in RETAIL_REC from -38.0% to -35.7% in the last week, if sustained for another week, indicates an intrinsic recovery trend that will lead to higher RETAIL_REC within the next week as consumer confidence improves.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC at t+1w is higher than RETAIL_REC at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC at t+1w is higher than t-0w, but the mean RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not higher than the mean of the previous 7 days.
